acv.quote: Two hundred and fifty K ACV.

data.reason: Halima, the COO, picked the rival because it named who would pick up on on-sale morning. Our support tiers sounded like 'a queue with a faster timer.' Jordan thought the load test won it.

trigger.action: Speak to the moment payments fail and nobody answers.
trigger.why: Payments failed four minutes into an arena on-sale. The old provider's ticket form replied after it ended.
trigger.quote: Their provider's support was a ticket form.

decider.action: Tell the COO exactly who answers when payments break.
decider.why: Halima, the COO, decided in one meeting. Ben, the CTO, wanted us but lost.
decider.quote: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting.

competitor.action: Answer 'who's my person' with named people, not support tiers.
competitor.why: Per Ben, the rival brought its named account team. Then Tixhaven's questions turned from throughput to names.
competitor.quote: Before that meeting it was throughput, queueing, bots. After, it was names.

message.action: Stop pitching support tiers and response times to operations leaders.
message.why: Jordan's walk through support tiers lost Halima. The load test Ben showed her only got 'good.'
message.quote: so it's a queue with a faster timer.

proof.action: Show on paper what we do on an on-sale morning.
proof.why: Halima asked who's watching and who she calls at minute four. We had only logos, no plan.
proof.quote: She wanted to see, on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning.

words.action: Swap 'uptime' and 'support' for 'what happens when it's down'.
words.why: Nobody at Tixhaven said 'support'. Halima said she pays for what happens during an outage.
words.quote: I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.
